Create a vertical 9:16 photorealistic personal vlog-style talking video driven by the uploaded reference audio.

Reference roles:
<Picture 1> is the complete visual reference for the single on-screen speaker and the environment. Preserve the person's exact facial identity, age, hairstyle, skin tone, clothing, body proportions and overall appearance. Preserve the original background, furniture, spatial layout, lighting, colors, camera angle and composition shown in Picture 1.

<Audio 1> is the only speech and performance-timing source. The person from Picture 1 speaks the exact words contained in Audio 1, following its original language, pronunciation, pacing, pauses, emotion and full duration. Synchronize the lip movements precisely with Audio 1. Do not rewrite, translate, summarize, repeat, extend or replace the spoken content. Do not generate any additional dialogue.

Style and performance:
Create a natural personal vlog recording, as if the person is speaking casually and directly to a smartphone camera. Show one person only. Preserve the original framing shown in Picture 1. The speaker maintains friendly and natural eye contact with the camera.

Include realistic blinking, breathing, subtle facial expressions, small natural head movements and restrained conversational gestures. Keep all gestures below shoulder level. Hands must never cover the mouth or face. The performance should feel relaxed, spontaneous and authentic rather than staged, cinematic or exaggerated.

Camera:
Use a stable smartphone vlog camera. Preserve the original camera position, viewing angle, framing and subject size shown in Picture 1. Do not zoom in, push in, pull out, orbit, pan, tilt, rotate, change angles, change focal length or transition into a close-up. Keep the person in the same position and at the same size throughout the video.

Continuity:
Use one continuous shot. Keep the same person, face, hairstyle, clothing, body proportions, background, furniture, lighting and camera perspective from the first frame to the last. Keep all background objects stationary. Only natural speaking movements should occur.

Audio:
Use Audio 1 as the only speech source and preserve its original timing, pronunciation, rhythm, pauses and emotion. Do not add music, background conversation, a second speaker, a newly generated voice or unintelligible vocal sounds.

Avoid subtitles, captions, text, logos, watermarks, cuts, scene changes, split screens, extra people, duplicate faces, identity drift, facial morphing, changing clothes, changing backgrounds, moving furniture, warped architecture, mouth distortion, frozen lips, excessive teeth, hands near the mouth, exaggerated gestures, rapid head turns, camera movement, zooming, push-ins, close-up transitions, camera shake, lip movement before speech begins or lip movement after speech ends.
